slides.title: Understanding the Product Proof of Concept (POC)
slides.body: An Initial Version of a Product Designed to Validate Feasibility
bullet_points: A POC is an initial version of a product designed to validate its feasibility.
It serves as a prototype that can demonstrate how the final product will look and function.
slides.speaker_notes: The purpose of a POC is to provide a practical demonstration of the product's concept without fully committing resources to development.

slides.title: Teacher Expectations and Control
bullet_points: Input learning objectives.
Define target audience levels (beginner, intermediate, advanced).
Set tone and style presets (formal, conversational, concise).
Specify structural directives (slide count, sections, emphasis).
Provide custom free-text prompts or extra instructions.
slides.speaker_notes: These controls help ensure that the generated content aligns with the teacher's expectations and provides a structured approach to content creation.

slides.title: Teacher Expectations and Control
slides.body: In this section, you will provide detailed guidance on how teachers set their expectations for students and manage classroom control.

slides.speaker_notes: For this part, it's crucial to ensure that all aspects align seamlessly with the target audience level of 'intermediate' and maintain a formal tone throughout.

slides.title: Post-POC Enhancements Overview
slides.body: This slide outlines key enhancements that have been made after the pilot project concluded.

slides.title: Adding Features to the POC
slides.body:
To ensure that the features selected for approval align with the intended audience and maintain clarity in communication, specific criteria must be set before approval.

During approval, an incremental approach is taken to introduce new features gradually without overwhelming the audience.
bullet_points: Set feature selection criteria before approval.
Implement an incremental feature addition strategy during approval.
